english: Please / you're welcome / here you go
note: Same word for all three.
Also how you get a waiter's attention.

english: Do you speak English? (to a man / to a woman)
hebrew: אתה מדבר אנגלית? / את מדברת אנגלית?
translit: ata medaber anglit? / at medaberet anglit?

note: Woman says: ani lo mevina.

english: I only speak a little Hebrew

note: In practice people just say Super-Pharm.
Emergency numbers: 100 police, 101 ambulance, 102 fire.

english: Can I have... / is it possible...?
note: The single most useful word. Efshar + noun = can I have it.
Woman says: ani rotsa.
To a woman: tni li.
To a woman: yesh lakh. To a shop: yesh lakhem.

english: Do you have...? (to a shop or restaurant)

note: Point and say et ze.
Literally upside-down.
Also written on menus as ais hafukh.
At Aroma and most chains ais kafe is the sweet blended slushy. For coffee over ice, ask for ais amerikano or hafukh kar.
Short espresso: espresso katsar.

english: Can I have a small iced latte with oat milk, to go?
hebrew: אפשר הפוך קר קטן עם שיבולת, לקחת?
translit: efshar hafukh kar katan im shibolet, lakakhat?
note: The whole order in one breath: efshar + drink + size + milk + lakakhat.

english: With oat milk / with soy milk
note: Full name on the carton: khalav shibolet shu'al. Nobody says it at the counter.

english: For here or to go? (they ask)

note: Literally can you pack it. Box is kufsa (קופסה).
Woman says: ani tsimkhonit.
Or just draw a signature in the air.
Ashrai alone means card.
Israeli cards can split purchases into installments. Answer ken.

english: Receipt / do you want a receipt?

note: Tip is usually 10 to 15 percent and not included.
Prices are spoken as just the number: esrim shekel.
Bags cost a few agorot.

english: Do you need a bag? (cashier asks)
Are you a club member? (cashier asks)
note: Loyalty card. Answer: lo.
Tens, then ve- plus the unit.
